fieldissues.issue: The medium calls a proposed military role a “massive violation” of the Posse Comitatus Act, while the long says the proposal raised a legal question and identifies statutory exceptions.
The long refers to “the available account” and repeats that the proposal was not implemented in its final sentence.

proposedchanges.description_medium: Replace “a massive violation of the Posse Comitatus Act” with “a proposal that raised questions under the Posse Comitatus Act, which generally limits domestic military law enforcement.”
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentence beginning “The available account does not describe” and the final sentence. State once that the statements were a proposal and that no deployment was reported.

evidencebasis: The Guardian source and latest long describe a transition proposal, not an issued order or deployment. The long also notes that the Act has exceptions.
notes: Keep the legal concern qualified and distinguish a campaign commitment from implemented policy.

fieldissues.issue: “Ends Birthright Citizenship” says the executive order achieved a change that courts blocked from taking effect.
“Blatant challenge,” “red meat political statement,” and “direct assault” are evaluative language; the medium should describe the order and its blocked status.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Orders Restriction on Birthright Citizenship; Courts Block Its Implementation
proposedchanges.description_medium: Replace the evaluative phrases with a concise account that Trump signed an order seeking to restrict citizenship for some U.S.-born children and courts blocked it from taking effect.

evidencebasis: The packet and latest long state that the order sought a restriction and federal courts enjoined implementation. The merged record retains the New York Times, White House order, and Supreme Court case URLs.
notes: The June 2025 injunction ruling was procedural and did not decide the order’s constitutionality.

fieldissues.issue: “Transition Team Fires” places the firings before Trump took office, while the merged account describes agency workforce reductions in February 2025.
The final paragraph tells the reviewer that the preserved title is wrong and distinguishes stages of the record instead of closing the event account.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Administration Fires Thousands of Probationary Federal Workers
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the final two sentences beginning “The reported effort began” and “Notices, completed separations.” Keep the distinction between termination notices, completed separations, and later court orders in the event chronology.

evidencebasis: The latest description and the three retained Guardian URLs place the reported firings after inauguration and document notices, reversals, and a temporary court block.
notes: Do not attribute the February 2025 workforce effort to the transition team or describe it as Schedule F without evidence.

fieldissues.issue: The title attributes a prosecution threat directly to Trump, while the long attributes the quoted “come after” and prosecute statement to Attorney General Pam Bondi.
The final two sentences repeat general commentary about threats, charges, and judicial independence rather than adding event detail.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Administration Officials Threaten Judges After Rulings Against Its Policies
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentences beginning “A threat by an executive official” and “The episode raises concerns.” Keep the reported Bondi statement, Trump’s attacks on named judges, and the attributed safety concerns.

evidencebasis: The supplied Guardian report and latest long attribute the quoted prosecution threat to Bondi and describe Trump’s attacks on judges. The Guardian URL is retained.
notes: Do not state that any judge faced a criminal charge or that investigators identified who coordinated threats at judges’ homes.

fieldissues.issue: “IG Massacre” is loaded language, and the title omits the event date needed to resolve the conflicting chronology.
The medium dates the firings to February 7, while the long dates them to January 24–25 and says the supplied link does not establish the later date.
The long says “I have retained that populated field,” an internal editorial note, and cites accessible reporting without supplying its URL.
The only packet URL is a January 21 New York Times link; the packet does not provide a source for the asserted January 24–25 chronology, later court ruling, or agency-specific effects.
The organization-tags field is null rather than an array.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Administration Dismisses About 17 Inspectors General
proposedchanges.description_medium: Use the event date only after an event-specific source confirms it. Attribute the count and congressional-notice claim to their sources; remove the unsupported appellate outcome and agency-impact claim unless sourced.
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the sentence beginning “The linked New York Times URL” and the sentence beginning “I have retained.” Add exact sources for the verified date, number dismissed, notice requirement, and any later court ruling.
proposedchanges.source_urls: Retain the New York Times URL only for claims it supports; add event-specific sources for the dismissal chronology and later litigation.

evidencebasis: The packet lists a January 21 New York Times article, while the latest medium says February 7 and the long says January 24–25. No other source URL is supplied to resolve that conflict.
notes: Do not publish a date, legal outcome, or agency-impact claim until the exact supporting source is available.
